correctness.rationale: Every finite one-point profile is an ideal/filter pair with lower points strictly below upper points. Defining a=I-1 and b=number of two-sided profiles yields t=2a+b+1. Parallel composition multiplies ideal counts and forces two-sided profiles into one component. Ordinal composition adds ideal counts with one overlap and partitions two-sided profiles into left-internal, right-internal, and nonempty lower-left/upper-right cross-profiles. These exhaustive bijections prove both recurrences by induction for arbitrary finite expression trees, including empty and singleton. The standalone direct-transitivity enumerator independently verifies all distinct binary-expression orders with 1–6 ordered leaves and 260 larger samples; this finite evidence corroborates, not replaces, the proof. Each count is at most 3^n, so exact arithmetic stays on O(n)-bit integers.

originality.rationale: The individual statements were compared by implication: the published general one-type result provides only the ideal/filter encoding and unrestricted hardness, not the two-state series/parallel formulas; the previously recorded ancestor-rooted-forest formula omits arbitrary N-free posets and the explicit diamond. A weak-order mapping-space recurrence counts a different object. The insertion-position work of Pretzel has a close object but its available abstract studies dimensions and restricted heights rather than this exact enumeration. No explicit prior theorem covering all series–parallel parameter posets with the two-state algebra was identified. This is best-knowledge originality, not proof of worldwide priority.

value.rationale: The class of N-free/series–parallel posets is natural, includes unrestricted nesting and width, and is much wider than the previously treated ancestor forests (for example, the four-element diamond). The result gives exact nonalgebraic 1-type counts with only two intrinsic states and O(n) arithmetic operations, contrasting with unrestricted #P-hard type counting. The recurrence exposes the distinct roles of series and parallel composition on two-sided insertion positions; it is a complete structural algorithm over a natural infinite class, not a bare table recomputation or minor boundary increment.
